data.mutability_note: The audit trail is append-only. There is no update or delete endpoint, and the database rejects both at the trigger level.

data.delivery_note: This queue is read on a short poll rather than pushed. There is no websocket channel, so a new request appears here within one poll interval, not instantly.

data.note: Demo photographs are generated by OpenCV. Findings produced from them are real pipeline output, not canned results.

scenarios.description: The same panel photographed twice with no change. The pipeline must report nothing; if it reports something here, it is producing false positives.
scenarios.label: No damage - identical conditions
scenarios.name: clean

scenarios.description: The pickup photo is 18% brighter, as if a cloud moved. Nothing changed on the vehicle. This is the scenario the lighting normalisation and diffuse-region filters exist to survive.
scenarios.label: Lighting change only - no damage
scenarios.name: lighting_only

scenarios.description: A thin scuff drawn along the lower door. Exercises the elongated, edge-dominant branch of the labeller.
scenarios.label: Scratch along the front door
scenarios.name: scratch

scenarios.description: A shading depression with no colour change. Exercises the dark-and-achromatic branch.
scenarios.label: Dent on the front wing
scenarios.name: dent

scenarios.description: A warm, mottled colour shift. Exercises the chroma channel, which is the only one that can see this at all.
scenarios.label: Rust patch on the lower wing
scenarios.name: rust

scenarios.description: A scratch, a dent and a paint chip, with the pickup frame shifted and rotated so alignment has to do real work. The fullest demonstration of the pipeline.
scenarios.label: Three defects, camera moved
scenarios.name: multiple

custody_duration.note: Distribution of hours between drop-off and pickup, in two-hour buckets. Shown as a distribution rather than an average because the long tail is what occupies bays.
custody_duration.title: Custody duration

damage_detections.note: Findings per week by verification outcome. CONFIRMED means a manager stood behind the detector; REJECTED means it was a false positive; UNVERIFIED means nobody has looked yet.
damage_detections.title: Damage detections

retrieval_time.note: Mean measured minutes from retrieval request to ready-for-pickup. Days with fewer than three retrievals are omitted rather than plotted, because a one-car average is not a trend.
retrieval_time.title: Average retrieval time

security_alerts.note: Alerts per ISO week, split by severity, with how many are still open. Weekly because alerts are sparse; a daily series would be mostly zeros.
security_alerts.title: Security alerts

vehicles_per_day.note: Tickets issued per calendar day. Days with no arrivals are zero, not gaps.
vehicles_per_day.title: Vehicles per day
